title: One ixdar-cli command to sweep models through a DSL graph and tabulate stages
user-messages:
> Every crawfish agent today wrote its own sweep scripts (sweep.sh, suite.sh, a stage-table script). One ixdar-cli command should run models through a DSL in one JVM, switching with the existing model route, and print a stage table with times and failures.

start a ticket on this
description:
Every crawfish agent on 2026-11-23/24 wrote its own sweep scripts to run many models through one DSL graph and tabulate how far each got: craw-146/tmp/scripts/{sweep,repair-sweep,suite,export}.sh and measurements.py, craw-143/tmp/{sweep,suite,spikes}.sh, the Blends check's run_one.py (with a quantization-stall watchdog), and earlier craw-141/142 copies. Each starts a new JVM per model, guesses timeouts, greps logs for the failure line and builds a stage table by hand; the tool review reports/tool-review-2026-11-24.md (items 2, 6, 7, 10) measured the cost.

Add one ixdar-cli command (e.g. `ixdar-cli model-sweep --graph <dsl template> --models <list|glob|suite|crawfish> [--stall S] [--timeout T] --out <dir>`) that runs each model through the graph in ONE scene JVM, switching models with the existing `model` route, and writes a table per model: input and repaired vertex/face counts, repair summary, cones/genus, furthest stage, failure message, quad count when it finishes, per-stage times (from mesh-dsl-timing), and a screenshot when it finishes. It takes a lock on its output directory, kills a model's run on a stall or timeout and records it, and names the suite and the crawfish scans as built-in model sets.
definition-of-done:
1. `ixdar-cli model-sweep` exists with --help, runs a list of models through a DSL graph in one JVM and writes the per-model table (markdown and JSON) plus screenshots for finished layouts.
2. Built-in model sets for the 11 quad-layout suite models and the ten crawfish scans.
3. Stalls and timeouts are recorded per model without stopping the sweep; a second writer to the same output directory is refused.
4. Measured: the ten crawfish scans and the suite sweep faster than the per-JVM scripts did (times before and after), and the output matches what those scripts reported.
5. Ixdar/CLAUDE.md is pointed at it when the user asks for that edit, so agents stop writing sweep scripts.
testing-plan:
1. Sweep the 11 suite models and compare counts with a run of the old scripts.
2. Sweep the ten crawfish scans with --stall 120 and check stalls are recorded.
changes-made: ixdar-cli model-sweep (ixdar_automation_cli/cli_commands/model_sweep.py): one quad-layout JVM for a list of models (sets suite and crawfish, names, globs, files) through a DSL template (built-ins layout, repair-layout), stall (branch-bound bound) and timeout kill with a fresh JVM for the next model, output-directory lock, sweep.md/sweep.json, per-model log slices and screenshots of finished layouts

New automation route mesh-dsl-stages (Stages.java): per-statement mesh counts, repair report, quad_layout furthest stage, cones, Euler characteristic, genus, quad and patch counts, node times; answers off the render thread

Measured: suite 30 s vs 114 s (per-JVM script) / 34 s (one-JVM script), counts identical; crawfish 1184 s vs 1293 s (583 vs 663 s without IMG_4113's 600 s cap), furthest stage and failure identical on all 10
review-summary: Adds `ixdar-cli model-sweep`, which runs a list of models through one DSL graph in a single quad-layout scene and writes a per-model stage table, backed by a new `mesh-dsl-stages` automation route. Agents no longer write their own sweep scripts, timeouts and log greps.
